newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello has not broken ministerial rules - PM.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello has not broken ministerial rules - PM.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello had not breached ministerial rules about conflict of interest by allowing his wife to keep shares in the Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Prime Minister John Howard said on Monday.
"In no way has he breached the guidelines," Howard told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.

"The interest of the day will be to see whether (Opposition Leader) Kim Beazley takes the (Opposition Treasury spokesman) Gareth Evans line and trys to pursue Tanya Costello because she owns a few hundred shares in the Commonwealth Bank," Howard said.
On Sunday the Assistant Treasurer Jim Short, the junior minister responsible for banking policy, resigned following controversy over his ownership of shares in ANZ Banking Group Ltd.

"It will be very interesting to see whether the party which has always tried to champion the independent personalities of women in our community is going to pursue the wife of the Treasurer because out of her own money in 1994, she bought several hundred shares in a float in which 100,000 of Australians participated," Howard said.

"I'll be fascinated to see whether Mr Beazley takes up the Evans mantra on this and criticises Tanya Costello, criticises Peter Costello, because I don't think either of them deserve any criticism at all," he said.

In a later interview on Australian Broadcasting Corp radio, Beazley did not criticise the Costellos, choosing instead to call for a revamp of the guidelines, which currently call for ministers to "have regard" for spouses shareholdings when deciding whether there was a conflict of interest.

But the guidelines do not require divestment of a spouses' shares, whereas ministers must divest their shares if there is a possible conflict of interest. "I don't think that this is a clear cut area at all," Beazley said.
"Spouses are entitled to their independence. We live in a different era from when many of these guidelines took their origins," Beazley said.

"What's required of Mr Howard is that he develop a far more clear cut set of considerations in relation to this, otherwise why have them in the guidelines, why have Mrs Anderson act in the way in which she did," he said.
The wife of Primary Industries Minister John Anderson sold her shares in building products and export woodchip company Boral Ltd when Anderson was making decisions on export licences.
Senator Brian Gibson, the parliamentary secretary to the Treasurer, has also said he would dispose of all his shares in the National Australia Bank Ltd and the Bank of Melbourne Ltd MBL.AX.
